```{r}
display_saved_image <- function(path, pending_message) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    knitr::include_graphics(path)
  } else {
    knitr::asis_output(paste0("<p><em>", pending_message, "</em></p>\n"))
  }
}

self_contained_iframe <- function(path, id, height, title, link_id) {
  escape_attribute <- function(value) {
    value <- gsub("&", "&amp;", value, fixed = TRUE)
    value <- gsub("\"", "&quot;", value, fixed = TRUE)
    value <- gsub("<", "&lt;", value, fixed = TRUE)
    gsub(">", "&gt;", value, fixed = TRUE)
  }

  payload <- paste(
    base64enc::base64encode(path, linewidth = 0),
    collapse = ""
  )
  frame_id <- escape_attribute(id)
  frame_title <- escape_attribute(title)
  fullscreen_id <- escape_attribute(link_id)

  paste0(
    "<script type='application/octet-stream' id='", frame_id,
    "-payload'>", payload, "</script>\n",
    "<iframe id='", frame_id, "' src='about:blank' ",
    "srcdoc=\"<p style='font:14px sans-serif;color:#626a75;",
    "padding:24px'>Loading interactive visual…</p>\" ",
    "width='100%' height='", as.integer(height), "' loading='lazy' ",
    "title='", frame_title, "'></iframe>\n",
    "<script>(function(){",
    "const frame=document.getElementById('", frame_id, "');",
    "const payload=document.getElementById('", frame_id, "-payload');",
    "const link=document.getElementById('", fullscreen_id, "');",
    "let url=null;",
    "const load=function(){",
    "if(url)return url;",
    "const binary=atob(payload.textContent.trim());",
    "const chunks=[];const chunkSize=1048576;",
    "for(let start=0;start<binary.length;start+=chunkSize){",
    "const end=Math.min(start+chunkSize,binary.length);",
    "const bytes=new Uint8Array(end-start);",
    "for(let i=start;i<end;i++)bytes[i-start]=binary.charCodeAt(i);",
    "chunks.push(bytes);}",
    "url=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob(chunks,{type:'text/html'}));",
    "frame.removeAttribute('srcdoc');frame.src=url;",
    "if(link)link.href=url;return url;};",
    "if(link)link.addEventListener('click',function(event){",
    "if(url)return;event.preventDefault();",
    "const popup=window.open('about:blank','_blank');",
    "const target=load();",
    "if(popup){popup.opener=null;popup.location=target;}});",
    "if('IntersectionObserver'in window){",
    "const observer=new IntersectionObserver(function(entries){",
    "if(entries.some(function(entry){return entry.isIntersecting;})){",
    "observer.disconnect();load();}},{rootMargin:'1000px 0px'});",
    "observer.observe(frame);}else{load();}})();</script>\n"
  )
}

display_widget <- function(path, pending_message) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    readRDS(path)
  } else {
    knitr::asis_output(paste0("<p><em>", pending_message, "</em></p>\n"))
  }
}

decision_of <- function(id) {
  if (is.null(battery)) return("pending")
  battery[hypothesis_id == id, decision][1]
}
```

# 2DG and seqFISH Co-embedding in Allen CCF

## Overview

This notebook treats the WildR-versus-SPF Intruder 2DG map as a **group-level**
contrast co-embedded with seqFISH NEUROeSTIMator activity in Allen CCFv3. The
upgrade adds what a controlled analysis requires: Baseline and within-genotype
Intruder−Baseline maps warped through the same Template transforms as
specificity controls, a pre-specified H1–H5 hypothesis battery with explicit
pass/fail language, and a wide interactive 3D CCF explorer (Baseline/Intruder
heatmaps, density controls, AP overlap, and region co-variation), plus a
front-to-back per-section registration QC browser.

```{r}
#| label: display-stats
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

n_accepted <- if (is.null(registration)) {
  0L
} else {
  sum(registration$accepted_final)
}
n_supported <- if (is.null(battery)) {
  0L
} else {
  sum(battery$decision == "supported")
}
n_tested <- if (is.null(battery)) 0L else nrow(battery)
cat("::: {.stat-row}\n")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[", n_accepted, "]{.stat-value}\n[Slices passing strict QC]{.stat-label}\n:::\n", sep = "")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[", n_tested, "]{.stat-value}\n[Pre-specified hypotheses]{.stat-label}\n:::\n", sep = "")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[", n_supported, "]{.stat-value}\n[Hypotheses supported]{.stat-label}\n:::\n", sep = "")
cat("::: {.stat}\n[3]{.stat-value}\n[Map families in CCF]{.stat-label}\n:::\n")
cat(":::\n")
```

## Background

Scalar `Template/` anatomy and `WildRvSPF Intruder/` t maps are the primary
inputs (`2DG = y/1.494`, `t = (y/18.409)−7.762`). Accepted Template→CCF warps
from [data/interim/2DG_CCF_Integration/2026-11-11]{.path} are reused—without
re-fitting Elastix—to place Baseline and WildR/SPF Intruder−Baseline RGB maps
into the same coordinates via the validated 254-color LUT. seqFISH still lacks
a verified section→animal key, so every cross-modality test remains
section/gate-level and non-animal.

## Hypotheses

These five claims were written before inspecting the control-map results. Only
they appear as findings.

| ID | Claim | Primary test | Control |
|----|-------|--------------|---------|
| H1 | Accepted Template slices occupy plausible CCF planes | Dice + AP continuity QC | Continuity gate retained |
| H2 | Positive Intruder \|t\| is enriched in a pre-specified limbic/hypothalamic annotation set | Set-vs-complement Δmean\|t\| + 10k label permutations | Same test on Baseline |
| H3 | Gate-allocated Intruder positive mean t correlates with NEUROeSTIMator Hedges' g | Spearman + gate permutation; α = 0.10 on this metric only | Baseline-allocated positive mean t |
| H4 | Intruder association is not explained by within-genotype Intruder−Baseline maps | \|ρ\|_Intruder vs max(\|ρ\|_WildR I−B, \|ρ\|_SPF I−B) with gate bootstrap | I−B maps |
| H5 | ROI seed footprints land in expected Allen parcels | Seed-slice IoU vs target parcels | Anatomical QC only |

::: {.figure-card}

[**Figure 0.**]{.fig-num} Pre-specified H1–H5 decision strip after control-map
inspection. Decisions are locked to the battery table; only these five claims
are promoted as findings.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Battery at a glance**

- **Supported:** H1 (registration QC), H3 (Intruder↔NE gate coupling).
- **Not supported:** H2 (limbic/hypothalamic \|t\| enrichment is Baseline-driven,
  not Intruder-specific).
- **Inconclusive:** H4 (SPF Intruder−Baseline nearly matches Intruder \|ρ\|);
  H5 (ROI seed footprints are not anatomical).
- **Scope.** All cross-modality tests are section/gate-level until a verified
  seqFISH section→animal key exists.
:::
:::

## Results

### H1 — Registration QC is tight where accepted

Each Template coronal slice was fit into Allen CCFv3 and scored by tissue Dice
against the atlas. A second gate rejects fits that would invent a discontinuous
anterior–posterior (AP) trajectory even when Dice is high. Only
`accepted_final` slices feed every downstream overlay, enrichment, and
co-embedding step. The browser below replaces the former Dice-by-slice summary:
it exposes the actual anatomy, warp, effect projection, and AP context for every
delivered section.

::: {.figure-card .fig-wide}
```{r}
#| label: display-h1-registration
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

    "target='_blank' rel='noopener'>Open registration QC fullscreen</a></p>"
  )
  cat(self_contained_iframe(
    registration_qc_html,
    "registration-qc-app",

    "registration-qc-fullscreen"

} else {
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 1.**]{.fig-num} Per-section Template→CCF registration audit. Move
front-to-back through all 66 delivered planes; toggle Intruder or Baseline.
Panels show original Template anatomy, source contrast, selected Allen plane,
warped-Template/Allen edge agreement, registered contrast, and sagittal/AP
trajectory context. Filters expose accepted versus withheld planes.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Decision: `r decision_of("H1")`**

- **How to review a plane.** Start with panels 1–3 to compare the delivered
  Template and contrast with the selected Allen anatomy. Panel 4 is the direct
  shape audit: cyan is warped Template tissue, orange is Allen tissue, and
  green marks edge agreement. Panel 5 verifies where the chosen contrast lands.
- **What was tested.** Accepted planes must pass tissue overlap, inside-atlas,
  and non-folding transform checks, then preserve a plausible front-to-back AP
  trajectory. Dice is shown as one metric in the browser, not as the visual
  conclusion.
- **Result.** 53/66 slices are `accepted_final` (mean Dice = 0.960). Twelve
  slices keep high Dice but fail AP continuity and are excluded. Template001 is
  blank and skipped.
- **Takeaway.** Use the **Rejected / blank** filter to inspect exactly what was
  withheld. No rejected plane contributes to regional summaries or the 3D
  co-embedding below.
:::
:::

### Interactive CCF co-embedding

Fixed-viewport Plotly explorer with symmetric Baseline / Intruder heatmaps,
CCF domain and subdomain surfaces, optional wire meshes and parcel borders,
seqFISH NEUROeSTIMator cells, shared density controls, and an AP window matched
to the registered seqFISH section band (~6725–7800 µm).

**How colors are generated.** 2DG clouds are colored by continuous signed t
(RdBu), drawn as a *random subsample of significant overlay voxels* — not
stratified by Allen region or cell type. **Blue = WildR higher; red = SPF higher.**
seqFISH points are colored by continuous NEUROeSTIMator `predicted_activity`
(Viridis), also a *random cell subsample* (seed 42).

**Hemisphere / mirror.** Seven seqFISH sections were registered with
`reflect=TRUE` in
[data/interim/registration/Allen_CCF_optimization/slice_positions_25um_final.xlsx]{.path}.
Viewer seqFISH coordinates use **anatomical ML** (those sections un-mirrored about
5700 µm). Provenance:
[tables/2DG_CCF_Integration/seqFISH_section_hemisphere_provenance_2026-11-14.csv]{.path};
plan:
[analysis_md/2DG_seqFISH_hemisphere_symmetry_plan.md]{.path}.

The redesigned anatomy controls are independent of the data controls. Choose
one 2DG contrast at a time (Intruder, Baseline, or none) to avoid ambiguous
overplotting; seqFISH remains an independent layer. A translucent whole-brain
surface can remain as context while a large Allen domain and one of its
subdomains are selected. The selected domain itself can be hidden while
retaining its subdomain. Surface, wire mesh, parcel points, and opacity can each
be changed without resetting the statistical data, density, or AP scope. The
curated colors and rendered surfaces follow the supplied
brainrender/BrainGlobe reference aesthetic.

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2.**]{.fig-num} Modular CCF explorer. A single selector switches
between Intruder and Baseline (or hides 2DG), while seqFISH is independently
available. The same density and AP-scope views apply to both 2DG contrasts.
Anatomical controls independently select whole-brain context, a large Allen
domain, a nested subdomain, surface, wire mesh, or parcel-border points. Camera
presets change orientation without changing any selected layer.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**What this explorer shows**

- **Same CCF frame.** Baseline and Intruder WildR−SPF heatmaps (RdBu; blue =
  WildR↑) sit with seqFISH NE cells (Viridis) and Allen anatomy (points or
  curated translucent region surfaces). Colors are random voxel/cell
  subsamples — not cell-type strata.
- **Symmetric controls.** Intruder and Baseline share one contrast selector and
  the same density, point-size, and AP-scope controls. Anatomy is separate:
  whole-brain context, selected domain, subdomain, surface, and wireframe can be
  changed without resetting the statistical data.
- **Why AP overlap matters.** Restricting to the seqFISH AP band
  (~6725–7800 µm) is the honest spatial comparison plane; full-brain clouds
  overstate co-localization.
- **Hemisphere.** Reflect=`TRUE` sections are un-mirrored to anatomical ML so
  left/right in the viewer match anatomy, not registration convenience.
- **Takeaway.** Use this for spatial intuition and QC of co-embedding — not as
  a substitute for the pre-specified H2–H5 tests below.
:::
:::

### Regional signature ranking and linked anatomy

The paired explorer below turns the same accepted CCF-registered 2DG maps into
an anatomical ranking and inspection tool. The left panel groups the currently
enabled Allen subdomains under 12 larger domains. Bars diverge around zero:
positive/blue is WildR-enriched and negative/red is SPF-enriched. The default
score is the voxel-weighted mean signed t among significant voxels from
accepted registrations. Domain summaries are calculated independently from
their Allen descendant IDs; they are not additive because some Allen hierarchy
composites overlap.

Clicking a bar links the rank to three complementary anatomical views. **3D
slices** shows significant voxels only on accepted coronal sections that
intersect the selected anatomy. **3D average** shades the selected mesh by its
descriptive mean t. **2D coronal** moves through all 66 delivered sections,
including rejected and blank inputs, with full Allen parcel context and the
selected domain/subdomain outlined. Rejected sections are shown for QC context
but never contribute to the ranking.

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2a.**]{.fig-num} Linked regional signature explorer. The diverging
bars rank the curated Allen domains and subdomains by accepted-map WildR−SPF
signal. Contrast, ranking direction, metric, minimum voxel coverage and number
of displayed subdomains are interactive. Bar selection drives the adjacent
3D slice evidence, descriptive mesh-average view and 66-section coronal atlas
browser.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**How to interpret this dashboard**

- **What the score measures.** Mean signed t is averaged across significant
  voxels assigned to the selected Allen hierarchy branch. `n_voxels`,
  `n_slices` and mean |t| are available as coverage and magnitude checks.
- **What it does not measure.** These are descriptive group statistical maps,
  not animal-level estimates. The source TIFFs do not contain parcel-level
  p values, FDR, standard errors or confidence intervals.
- **Why the views differ.** The 3D modes use accepted registrations only. The
  2D browser deliberately retains all delivered sections so rejected,
  continuity-withheld, blank and missing-Baseline inputs remain auditable.
- **How to use ranks.** Sort by WildR, SPF or absolute difference to find
  anatomical candidates, then inspect their spatial support before drawing a
  biological conclusion. A strong bar supported by few voxels or one section
  should be treated cautiously.
:::
:::

### Per-region NE vs 2DG co-variation

Allen parcels present in both seqFISH and 2DG overlays (≥100 seqFISH cells and
≥10 Intruder overlay pixels; n = 137 after filters). Each point is one
annotation: descriptive NEUROeSTIMator WildR−SPF Δ vs Intruder mean t, Baseline
mean t, and Baseline vs Intruder. Orange marks the pre-specified
limbic/hypothalamic set used in H2.

```{r}
#| label: display-covariation-stats
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

if (!is.null(covariation) && nrow(covariation) > 2L) {
  rho_i <- cor.test(
    covariation$intruder_mean_t,
    covariation$seqfish_wildr_minus_spf_descriptive,
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )
  rho_b <- cor.test(
    covariation$baseline_mean_t,
    covariation$seqfish_wildr_minus_spf_descriptive,
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )
  rho_bi <- cor.test(
    covariation$baseline_mean_t,
    covariation$intruder_mean_t,
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )
  cat(
    "<p>Filtered regions = ", nrow(covariation),
    "; Spearman ρ(NE Δ, Intruder t) = ", sprintf("%.3f", unname(rho_i$estimate)),
    " (p = ", format.pval(rho_i$p.value, digits = 3), ")",
    "; ρ(NE Δ, Baseline t) = ", sprintf("%.3f", unname(rho_b$estimate)),
    " (p = ", format.pval(rho_b$p.value, digits = 3), ")",
    "; ρ(Baseline t, Intruder t) = ", sprintf("%.3f", unname(rho_bi$estimate)),
    " (p = ", format.pval(rho_bi$p.value, digits = 3), "). ",
    "Positive on either axis = WildR higher.</p>\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

::: {.takeaways}
**Co-variation takeaways**

- **NE vs Intruder.** Weak / non-significant (ρ ≈ −0.12, p ≈ 0.16): regional
  Intruder 2DG polarity does **not** track descriptive NE Δ at the parcel level.
- **NE vs Baseline.** Modest positive association (ρ ≈ 0.25, p ≈ 0.0037):
  Baseline WildR−SPF structure is the map that better co-varies with NE here —
  consistent with H2’s Baseline-driven limbic enrichment story.
- **Baseline vs Intruder.** Negative (ρ ≈ −0.34, p ≈ 3.8×10⁻⁵): the two 2DG
  contrasts are not the same spatial polarity across parcels.
- **Scope.** Descriptive region-level only — not animal-level inference. Table:
  [tables/2DG_CCF_Integration/2DG_region_covariation_2026-11-21c.csv]{.path}.
:::
:::

### Hemisphere symmetry signatures

Full-brain 2DG voxels are labeled left/right at midline 5700 µm. seqFISH uses
**anatomical** ML after un-mirroring `reflect=TRUE` sections. Regions are classed
**symmetric / unilateral / opposing / indeterminate** with locked thresholds
(2DG τ=0.75 / τ0=0.25; NE τ=0.004 / τ0=0.0015; δ=0.35). Descriptive only — not
animal-level.

::: {.figure-card}
```{r}
#| label: display-symmetry-counts
#| echo: false
#| out.width: "70%"
#| fig.align: "center"

display_saved_image(
  symmetry_counts_figure,
  "Symmetry class-count figure not yet written."
)
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2c.**]{.fig-num} Counts of hemisphere symmetry classes for Baseline 2DG,
Intruder 2DG, and NEUROeSTIMator WildR−SPF regional effects.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Class counts**

- **What was done.** Locked thresholds applied after anatomical ML annotation;
  classes locked before inspecting per-region strips.
- **Pattern.** Indeterminate dominates all three maps (sparse sides / weak
  bilateral effects). Among classifiable Intruder parcels: mostly symmetric,
  with smaller unilateral and opposing tails.
- **Takeaway.** Hemisphere structure is measurable but sparse — do not over-read
  bilateral symmetry as the main WildR−SPF story.
:::
:::

::: {.figure-card}
```{r}

#| echo: false

)
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2d.**]{.fig-num} Per-region signature strip (limbic / non-indeterminate
focus). Full table:
[tables/2DG_CCF_Integration/2DG_NE_hemisphere_symmetry_classes_2026-11-14e.csv]{.path}.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Signature strip**

- **What it shows.** Baseline / Intruder / NE class for limbic and other
  non-indeterminate parcels side-by-side.
- **Conclusion.** Class agreement across maps is incomplete — a region can be
  symmetric on Intruder and indeterminate or opposing on NE. Use the CSV for
  parcel-level follow-up; this strip is a compact audit, not a hypothesis test.
:::
:::

::: {.figure-card}
```{r}
#| label: display-symmetry-lat
#| echo: false
#| out.width: "72%"
#| fig.align: "center"

display_saved_image(
  symmetry_lat_figure,
  "Lateralization concordance figure not yet written."
)
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 2e.**]{.fig-num} Lateralization-index concordance: NE vs Intruder and NE
vs Baseline. Index = (R−L)/(|R|+|L|); positive = right-biased WildR−SPF effect.
:::

```{r}
#| label: display-symmetry-stats
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

if (!is.null(symmetry) && nrow(symmetry) > 2L) {
  ok <- symmetry[is.finite(intruder_lat_index) & is.finite(ne_lat_index)]
  rho_i <- if (nrow(ok) > 5L) {
    cor(ok$intruder_lat_index, ok$ne_lat_index, method = "spearman")
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  okb <- symmetry[is.finite(baseline_lat_index) & is.finite(ne_lat_index)]
  rho_b <- if (nrow(okb) > 5L) {
    cor(okb$baseline_lat_index, okb$ne_lat_index, method = "spearman")
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
  cat(
    "<p>Regions in concordance table = ", nrow(symmetry),
    ". Intruder classes: symmetric ",
    sum(symmetry$twodg_intruder_symmetry_class == "symmetric", na.rm = TRUE),
    ", unilateral ",
    sum(symmetry$twodg_intruder_symmetry_class == "unilateral", na.rm = TRUE),
    ", opposing ",
    sum(symmetry$twodg_intruder_symmetry_class == "opposing", na.rm = TRUE),
    ". Spearman ρ(lat Intruder, lat NE) = ", sprintf("%.3f", rho_i),
    "; ρ(lat Baseline, lat NE) = ", sprintf("%.3f", rho_b),
    ".</p>\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

::: {.takeaways}
**Lateralization concordance**

- **Intruder ↔ NE.** Weak positive concordance of lateralization indices
  (ρ ≈ 0.19) — some shared left/right bias, far from a tight match.
- **Baseline ↔ NE.** Essentially flat (ρ ≈ 0.04).
- **Method note.** Do **not** force every seqFISH section onto one CCF side;
  annotate `reflect` and use anatomical ML
  ([analysis_md/2DG_seqFISH_hemisphere_symmetry_plan.md]{.path}).
- **Still open.** H2–H4 re-test with an explicit hemisphere factor; animal-level
  models once a section→animal key exists.
:::
:::

### H2 — Limbic/hypothalamic enrichment is Baseline-like, not Intruder-specific

H2 asked whether **Intruder** WildR−SPF \|t\| is enriched inside a
pre-specified limbic/hypothalamic Allen annotation set relative to the rest of
the brain. For each map we compute Δmean\|t\| = mean\|t\|(set) −
mean\|t\|(complement), then permute annotation labels 10,000 times within that
map. The same test on the **Baseline** map is the control: Intruder enrichment
must exceed Baseline to count as Intruder-specific.

::: {.figure-card}
```{r}
#| label: display-h2
#| echo: false
#| out.width: "48%"
#| fig.align: "center"

display_saved_image(
  h2_figure,
  "H2 enrichment figure not yet written."
)
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 3.**]{.fig-num} Pre-specified limbic/hypothalamic set versus
complement: Δ mean \|t\| for Intruder and Baseline (10k label permutations).
Positive = higher mean \|t\| inside the set.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Decision: `r decision_of("H2")`**

- **Intruder.** Δmean\|t\| = −0.032 (p ≈ 0.85; 62 set / 572 complement parcels):
  no enrichment in the pre-specified set under the social Intruder contrast.
- **Baseline control.** Δmean\|t\| = +0.63 (p ≈ 0.0003; 53 / 336): the same
  limbic/hypothalamic set is strongly enriched on the home-cage Baseline map.
- **Conclusion.** Limbic/hypothalamic \|t\| concentration is a **Baseline**
  property of the WildR−SPF difference, not an Intruder-specific signature.
  H2’s control requirement (Intruder stronger than Baseline) fails, so the
  claim is not supported.
:::
:::

### H3 — Intruder positive mean t tracks gated NEUROeSTIMator g; Baseline does not

H3 links **seqFISH NEUROeSTIMator** (excitability proxy; Hedges’ g WildR−SPF per
`final_gate`) to **gate-allocated positive mean 2DG t**. For each gate we take
voxels whose strongest positive t falls in that gate’s allocation, then
Spearman-correlate those scores with NE g across gates (n = 10). Pre-declared
α = 0.10 on the Intruder metric only. Controls: the same allocation on
Baseline, plus within-genotype Intruder−Baseline maps (WildR and SPF).

::: {.figure-card}
```{r}
#| label: display-h3-triad
#| echo: false
#| out.width: "68%"
#| fig.align: "center"

display_saved_image(
  triad_figure,
  "Control-triad figure not yet written."
)
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 4.**]{.fig-num} Control triad: gate-allocated positive mean t versus
NEUROeSTIMator Hedges’ g for Intruder, Baseline, WildR Intruder−Baseline, and
SPF Intruder−Baseline. Each point is one `final_gate`.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Decision: `r decision_of("H3")`**

- **Intruder.** Spearman ρ = −0.661 (permutation p ≈ 0.041): gates with
  stronger WildR>SPF NE activity tend to carry **lower** mean positive Intruder
  2DG t under gate allocation (negative coupling, not “hotter Intruder where
  NE is higher”).
- **Baseline control.** ρ = +0.139 (p ≈ 0.70) — the association **collapses**
  on Baseline, so it is not a generic WildR−SPF map artifact.
- **I−B panels.** Within-genotype Intruder−Baseline maps are the H4 bridge:
  SPF I−B nearly matches Intruder \|ρ\| (see below), so interpret H3 as
  Intruder-associated but not cleanly genotype-isolated.
- **Conclusion.** Supported at the pre-declared α for Intruder vs NE, with the
  sign and Baseline collapse as the main scientific content — not a simple
  “co-activation” story.
:::
:::

```{r}
#| label: display-gate-triad-table
#| echo: false

if (!is.null(gate_triad)) {
  knitr::kable(
    gate_triad[
      order(neuro_hedges_g),
      .(
        final_gate,
        neuro_hedges_g,
        intruder_positive_mean_t,
        baseline_positive_mean_t,
        wildr_ib_positive_mean_t,
        spf_ib_positive_mean_t
      )
    ],
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Control triad of gate-allocated positive mean t scores."
  )
}
```

### H4 — Within-genotype Intruder−Baseline partially overlaps the Intruder signal

H4 asks whether the H3 Intruder↔NE association is **stronger** than the same
association built from within-genotype Intruder−Baseline (I−B) 2DG maps. If SPF
or WildR I−B matches or beats Intruder \|ρ\|, the WildR−SPF Intruder map is not
cleanly separable from context-driven structure.

::: {.takeaways}
**Decision: `r decision_of("H4")`**

- **What was compared.** \|ρ\|_Intruder = 0.661 vs \|ρ\|_SPF I−B = 0.636 and
  \|ρ\|_WildR I−B = 0.115 (gate-level, same NE g vector).
- **Stability.** Intruder only barely exceeds the stronger I−B map
  (Δ ≈ 0.024); bootstrap P(Δ ≤ 0) ≈ 0.64, so the excess is not reliable.
- **Conclusion.** Inconclusive for “Intruder-specific beyond context.” Treat
  H3 as Intruder-associated but **not** genotype-isolated until I−B structure
  is resolved (ideally with scalar I−B exports and an animal-level key).
:::

### H5 — ROI seed footprints are not yet anatomically diagnostic

H5 is **spatial QC**, not a biology claim: do WildR Intruder ROI overlay
footprints on seed slices land in the expected Allen parcels (IoU vs target
labels), using only `accepted_final` planes?

::: {.figure-card}
```{r}
#| label: display-h5
#| echo: false
#| out.width: "52%"
#| fig.align: "center"

display_saved_image(
  roi_figure,
  "ROI seed overlap figure not yet written."
)
```

::: {.fig-caption}
[**Figure 5.**]{.fig-num} IoU of WildR Intruder ROI overlay footprints versus
expected Allen parcels on seed slices. Planes that fail continuity QC are
excluded from the mean.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
**Decision: `r decision_of("H5")`**

- **Coverage.** Only 3/6 seed slices are `accepted_final`; among usable seeds,
  mean IoU ≈ 0.004, and only R_vHPC shows non-zero overlap (~0.013).
- **Misses.** L_LS and R_Cg footprints under the current AP assignment do not
  land in septal / cingulate parcels (IoU = 0).
- **Conclusion.** Inconclusive as anatomical masks. Do **not** use these ROI
  overlays to claim parcel-localized Intruder biology until footprints are
  rebuilt or confirmed as true anatomical ROIs rather than contrast displays.
:::
:::

### Findings

Synthesizing the co-embedding, regional co-variation, hemisphere audit, and
pre-specified battery:

1. **H1 supported.** Strict Template→CCF registration yields 53 accepted slices
   at mean Dice 0.960 with an intact continuity gate — the shared coordinate
   frame for everything above is trustworthy where used.
2. **H2 not supported.** Limbic/hypothalamic \|t\| enrichment is a **Baseline**
   property (Δ ≈ +0.63, p ≈ 0.0003), not Intruder-specific (Δ ≈ −0.03, p ≈ 0.85).
   Parcel-level NE↔2DG co-variation (Fig. 2b) points the same way.
3. **H3 supported.** Gate-allocated Intruder positive mean t correlates with
   NEUROeSTIMator Hedges’ g (ρ = −0.66, p ≈ 0.041); Baseline does not. The
   negative sign is part of the result, not a labeling error.
4. **H4 inconclusive.** SPF Intruder−Baseline nearly matches Intruder \|ρ\|, so
   genotype WildR−SPF Intruder is not cleanly isolated from context-driven
   structure.
5. **H5 inconclusive.** ROI seed overlays do not currently provide trustworthy
   anatomical parcel footprints under accepted CCF planes.

::: {.callout-warning}
None of these tests are animal-level. 2DG remains a group map; seqFISH still
lacks a verified section→animal key. Do not promote H3 to a confirmatory
genotype effect without that key and without resolving H4.
:::

## Next Steps

- Obtain a verified seqFISH section→animal key before any inferential cross-modality model.
- Resolve H4 with scalar (non-RGB) Intruder−Baseline exports if available.
- Revisit ROI overlays only after confirming they are anatomical masks rather than contrast displays.
- Optionally warp Behavior stacks under the same Template transforms as a separate map family.
